text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache slab churn detected in region us-east-1. p99 latency for streaming RPCs > 2s for the last 5m. Paging on-call. Incident ID: INC-2026-5100

sara: on it, saw the paging. I'm pulling the grafana panels now — kv-prefill eviction spikes + decode miss rate jump around 19:04 UTC.

mike: same here, seeing streaming stalls in traces. A lot of tails hitting decode path slower than usual. p95 ~800ms -> 1.6s, p99 up to 2.4s.

jordan: tagging logs and traces: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-cache?view=recent (link from alert).

sara: important note: eviction rate for prefill entries is 3x baseline. prefill insertion rate hasn't changed much, but slab fragmentation increased — small entries taking many slabs.

mike: TL;DR hypothesis: KV slab fragmentation -> frequent eviction -> prefill entries evicted before decode can reuse -> decode falls back to full model path -> tail latency. Also streaming backend queues up because KV misses slow downstream.

lee: customer impact check: no full outage, but streaming sessions for some enterprise customers show significant tail stalls and reconnects. Support ticketing shows elevated complaints for provider "Chatly" test accounts.

ops-bot: Affected infra: inference-pool-us-east-1 (gpu-cluster-a), kv-cache-shard-{12..15}. Host metrics attached in alert.

sara: I ran a quick acceptance query on shard 13: `kvctl metrics shard 13 --window 10m` — eviction_rate: 185/s, avg_slab_util: 0.27, prefill_hit_rate: 0.41 -> baseline 0.78. decode_miss_latency p99=2200ms.

mike: thanks. Can we confirm prefill vs decode imbalance? check trafficsource: prefill latency hasn't increased, but prefill eviction count went way up at the same time as decode misses. That matches.

jordan: rolling mitigation options: 1) increase slab allocation / temporarily enlarge pool to reduce eviction. 2) force-prefill-throttle for long-context requests. 3) route heavy streaming customers to a different pool (fallback). Which to prioritize?

sara: quick and low-risk: bump slab_max for affected shards by 20% to absorb churn while we investigate fragmentation cause. I'm preparing the kvctl command.

mike: agree. Also toggle prefill-priority to favor prefill entries over decode entries for 10m to see immediate hit-rate improvement. That should reduce tail stalls.

ops-bot: proposed commands (dry-run):
```
# increase slab cap for shard 12-15
kvctl set slab_cap --shards 12,13,14,15 --factor 1.2 --reason "INC-2026 emergency slab bump"
# favor prefill for short window
kvctl set policy --name prefill_priority --value high --duration 600
```

sara: executing now on shard 13 first, will watch metrics.

sara: DONE: `kvctl set slab_cap --shards 13 --factor 1.2 --reason INC-2026` (19:12:27 UTC). Watching.

mike: also pushed `kvctl set policy prefill_priority high --duration 600` (19:12:40 UTC).

ops-bot: Command accepted. Changes propagating to kv-proxies.

jordan: visual checks?

sara: prefill_hit_rate on shard 13 jumped to 0.66 within 30s, eviction_rate down 40%. p99 decode latency dropped from 2200ms -> 900ms within 90s. Streaming stall traces show fewer queue stalls.

lee: that's promising. Customer complaints rate decreased on Chatly test suite. Not fully resolved but lower error/retry count.

mike: ok this confirms eviction pressure was primary. Next step: identify why fragmentation spiked. Any recent deployments or workload changes?

sara: I checked deploys feed — no kv-side deploys in the 2 hours before spike. There's a spike in long-context streaming requests from a single customer IP block starting 18:58 UTC — likely larger documents causing many small prefill inserts.

jordan: could be a change in client behavior or a load-test. Ops, can we look up which account/hits?

ops-bot: top offending tenant: tenant-4772 (approx 28% of prefill insert churn). Request patterns: lots of small keys ~ 256B inserted rapidly.

mike: if tenant-4772 is responsible, we should throttle them temporarily while we do fragmentation remediation. Options: routing to dedicated fallback pool or apply per-tenant throttle.

lee: pinged CS to reach out to tenant-4772. They may be running a new ingestion job.

sara: medium-term fix: we need to tune slab allocator heuristics to better pack small entries (compaction) or adjust eviction priority to avoid prefill eviction before decode reuse. I'll open a follow-up ticket. For now continue mitigation.

jordan: risk check for increasing slab cap: memory pressure? Any risk of OOM?

ops-bot: current mem headroom on affected hosts ~22%. With 1.2x slab cap for shards 12-15 we estimate 6-8% increase usage — within margin. We'll monitor.

mike: good. After 10m tests, we should roll the slab bump to remaining shards if improvement holds. Also add a temporary routing rule to divert streaming-heavy clients to a different pool.

sara: I've extended prefill_priority another 10m (executed 19:19:52 UTC). Eviction rate continues down on 12-15. p95 trending toward baseline.

lee: CS reports tenant-4772 acknowledged and paused their ingestion job for 15m. That helps.

jordan: decision log for incident: 1) immediate slab cap bump (shard 13 then 12,14,15), 2) raise prefill_priority for 20m, 3) request tenant pause, 4) on-call follow-up to implement allocator compaction ticket.

mike: I'll draft the incident summary and SLO impact: p99 SLO breached for ~8 minutes from 19:04->19:12 peak, with partial mitigation reducing severity. We'll compute token-level customer impact and add to postmortem.

sara: applying slab bump to shards 12,14,15 now (19:22:15 UTC).

ops-bot: slab cap commands accepted for 12,14,15.

sara: monitoring all affected metrics: eviction_rate cluster-wide for these shards down ~55%, prefill hit rate improving, decode p99 now 720ms.

lee: can we remove the temporary routing after things stabilize? We probably don't need it now.

jordan: yes remove once 30m of stable metrics. I'll own that timer.

mike: handoff: I'm on-call until 20:00 UTC; Jordan you'll take over after?

jordan: I can take the formal handoff at 20:00 UTC. Sara, please include the small diagnostic commands and the kvctl history in the postmortem.

sara: adding `kvctl audit --since 19:00 --until 19:30 --inc-id INC-2026` to the ticket.

ops-bot: NOTE: No further regressions in the last 8m. Continuing to monitor.

lee: quick customer note for CS: impact limited to increased latency and transient stalls for some streaming sessions between 19:04-19:25 UTC. No data loss reported. CS queued note to tenants.

mike: assigning follow-ups: ENG-ALLOC-812 (allocator compaction), ENG-ROUTING-407 (per-tenant throttles / routing safeguards), ENG-METRICS-998 (add slab fragmentation alert).

jordan: final status update (19:32 UTC): mitigations succeeded, system stable, on-call handoff at 20:00 UTC. Will prepare incident postmortem template and invite relevant owners.

sara: thanks all. I'm marking as "mitigated" in the incident tracker and starting the postmortem draft.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-5100 status -> MITIGATED (19:32:10 UTC)."
